_readme: THE APP STORE AGE-RATING ANSWERS — Nikatru Subscription Tracker, channel `ios-appstore`.
🔴 THIS FILE RECORDS ANSWERS. IT DOES NOT RECORD A RATING, AND IT MUST NOT. Apple computes the
age rating from these answers; the developer supplies the answers and never the number. A rating
written here before the declaration has been submitted would be a value nobody computed, sitting
in the repository looking authoritative. `assignedRating` is therefore null and `status` says why.
This mirrors android-play/content-rating.json exactly, for the same reason it gives.
⚠️ THE ATTRIBUTE NAMES BELOW ARE APPLE'S DOCUMENTED App Store Connect API FIELDS AND ARE
UNVERIFIED AGAINST THIS ACCOUNT. Measured 2026-09-12 with the ASC API key in the vault: a signed
ES256 request to GET /v1/apps returned HTTP 200 with ZERO app records, so there is no appInfo and
therefore no live `ageRatingDeclaration` resource to read the real field set from. The names here
are from Apple's published API reference, NOT from this account. The first app record created will
expose the live set; if a name differs, THIS FILE IS WRONG AND THE LIVE ONE IS RIGHT.
📌 WHY IT EXISTS BEFORE THERE IS AN APP RECORD: O-APPLE-AGE-RATINGS. Apple requires age-rating
answers on submissions from September 2026. The answers are a property of what the app DOES, which
is knowable now and is cheaper to derive now than under submission pressure.
HAND-OWNED. [ADR 037]: "a sworn declaration regenerated by a template is a statement nobody made."
tooling/app-yaml/render.mjs must never write this file.

⏱ 2026-09-12: `unrestricted-web-access` was written as needs-verification and has since been MEASURED — see its note. The two remaining `stated-not-derived` claims (contests, medical information) have no dependency tell by nature and are recorded as statements rather than dressed up as measurements.
statusReason: No app record exists in App Store Connect. Measured 2026-09-12: a signed ES256 request to GET /v1/apps returned HTTP 200 and `data` was empty, so the declaration cannot be submitted and no rating can exist. The answers below are prepared; submitting them is a per-app Console or API action that follows the first app record, and publishing is the owner's word alone (C-MANUAL-FIRST-PUBLISH).

audienceFloor.source: [ADR 068] — no NIKATRU app, extension or site targets children; the audience floor is 18
audienceFloor.consequence: Every answer below is consistent with an adult-only audience, and NO Kids Age Band is declared. [ADR 068] forbids building age gates or Families/Kids declarations, so `kidsAgeBand` is null by decision rather than by omission.

questionnaireWording.why: Apple renders the age-rating questionnaire inside App Store Connect for an app record that does not exist yet, and the API resource that would carry the live attribute names (ageRatingDeclaration) hangs off an appInfo this account has none of. The wording and the exact attribute set are therefore UNVERIFIED. Re-read them from the live declaration once the first app record exists and correct this file against it — the live set wins.
questionnaireWording.measuredBy: GET /v1/apps with an ES256 JWT signed by APPLE_ASC_KEY_ID -> HTTP 200, data: []

claims.claim: The app contains no violence of any kind.
claims.note: Carried from android-play/content-rating.json claim `content-descriptors`, which derives it from dependency tells over the same Dart source. One app, one binary set of behaviours; re-deriving it here from the same tells would be a second copy of one measurement.

claims.claim: The app contains no sexual content or nudity.
The app contains no profanity or crude humour.
The app contains no use of, or reference to, alcohol, tobacco or drugs.
The app contains no horror, fear or mature/suggestive themes.
The app contains no gambling, simulated gambling, loot boxes or real-money wagering.
claims.note: android-play/content-rating.json claim `gambling` derives this from dependency tells.

claims.claim: The app runs no contests, sweepstakes or prize draws.
claims.note: ⚠️ NOT MECHANICALLY DERIVED. There is no dependency tell for a contest — it is a product decision, not a library. It is true of the app as designed today and it is recorded as a STATEMENT rather than dressed up as a measurement.

claims.claim: The app provides no medical or treatment information.
claims.note: A subscription tracker records billing dates and amounts. Nothing in it advises on health.

claims.claim: The app embeds NO browser. Every outbound link is handed to the SYSTEM browser and the URL set is first-party only.
claims.note: MEASURED 2026-09-12, so this is no longer the open question it was written as. Every launchUrl call site in the app passes LaunchMode.externalApplication — apps/subscriptiontracker/lib/app.dart:216, features/settings/settings_screen.dart:1152, features/shared/widgets.dart:750 — which hands the URL to the system browser and renders nothing in-app. There is no WebView widget in the app at all. The URLs reachable from the source are first-party only: nikatru.com and its /privacy, /terms, /refund, /contact and /checkout-return paths, plus config.nikatru.com. Apple treats an EMBEDDED browser as unrestricted web access; handing a fixed first-party URL to the OS is not one.

claims.claim: Users cannot interact with, message or exchange content with other users. There is no social surface.
The app contains no advertising of any kind, and no advertising or attribution SDK.
claims.note: android-play/content-rating.json claim `contains-ads`, derived from dependency tells; android-play/ads-declaration.json is the sworn form of the same fact.

claims.claim: The app offers in-app purchases: its own premium subscription.
claims.note: [ADR 078] — Android and iOS sell subscriptions IN-APP at v1, reversing ADR 059 Shape A. This is the one YES in the set and it is a decision rather than a dependency tell.

claims.claim: No Kids Age Band is declared.
claims.note: [ADR 068] sets the audience floor at 18 and forbids Families/Kids declarations outright. Null here is a decision, not an omission.
